approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would create a Bill of Rights in Australian law.
It would invalidate any Commonwealth, state or territory law that conflicts with the Bill of Rights and require those laws to be interpreted consistently with it.
The Australian Human Rights Commission could investigate acts or practices that may breach a right or freedom in the Bill of Rights and handle complaints about such breaches.
Invalidate inconsistent Commonwealth, state and territory laws.
Require Commonwealth, state and territory laws to be interpreted consistently with the Bill of Rights.
Allow the Australian Human Rights Commission to investigate acts or practices that may infringe a right or freedom.
Allow complaints to be made to the Commission alleging an infringement of a right or freedom.
Commonwealth, state and territory governments and the Australian Human Rights Commission.

Seconded the Australian Bill of Rights Bill, arguing the government's postal survey on LGBTI rights and citizenship rule changes infringe human rights, and called for a national approach to human rights legislation.
